prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right one depends on your ZIP code, age/family size, income (subsidy eligibility), health needs, and whether you want in‑person help. I can pick specific, highly rated local brokers for you if you tell me your ZIP code and whether you need individual/family, dental, Medicare, etc. Meanwhile, here’s a practical guide to find the best broker in Kansas City, MO and what to look for.

How to find brokers who work well for self‑employed people
- Use the federal marketplace local help tool (HealthCare.gov “Find Local Help”) for certified agents/navigators who know ACA subsidies.
- Use NAHU’s “Find an Agent” or the Missouri Department of Insurance directory to verify licenses.
- Check independent online brokers that compare multiple carriers (e.g., HealthSherpa, eHealth) if you want quick side‑by‑side quotes.
- Read local Google/Yelp reviews and ask other self‑employed people or small business groups in KC for referrals.

What to prefer in a broker for someone self‑employed
- Experience with individual ACA marketplace plans and premium tax credit/subsidy eligibility.
- Independent (represents multiple carriers) rather than captive (tied to one insurer).
- Transparent about how they’re paid (commission vs fee) and about renewal/plan change support.
- Good reviews for responsiveness and claim/renewal help.
- Able to advise on small‑group options, association plans, HSAs, and cost‑saving strategies for the self‑employed.

Questions to ask any broker before you hire them
- Do you specialize in individual/marketplace plans for self‑employed clients?
- Which carriers do you represent? Are you independent?
- How do you get paid? Will I be charged any fees?
- Can you check subsidy eligibility and help me apply through the marketplace?
- Will you help with renewals and claims, or only initial enrollment?
- Can you provide references from other self‑employed clients?

Quick suggestions for next steps
- Tell me your ZIP code, ages (self + dependents), and estimated household income and I’ll pull a short list of well‑rated local brokers and national comparison options that fit your needs.
- Or go to HealthCare.gov → “Find Local Help” and NAHU.org to contact agents immediately.

If you want, provide your ZIP code and a couple details (individual vs family, income range, in‑network providers you must keep), and I’ll find 3–5 Kansas City brokers/agencies to contact and include summary notes and contact questions.
